children.approach: Huh-Hwang-Kim-Kim-Oh Theorem 3.7: any function f: H -> A satisfying the restricted modular law is uniquely determined by its values f(p_{n_1}+...+p_{n_d}) on disjoint unions of paths. Algorithm 3.5 is the explicit reduction via Lemmas 3.3 (flat case) and 3.4 (non-flat case).

X_G (chromatic quasisymmetric) satisfies the full modular law (Guay-Paquet 2013 for the original CSF; Abreu-Nigro for CQSF). A fortiori X_G satisfies the restricted modular law of HHKKO. Combined with HHKKO Thm 3.7, this gives Rick's hunch as an immediate corollary.

Direct SymPy computation: for all 9 iso types of unit-interval graphs on 4 vertices, X_G expressed as integer linear combination of {X_{P_lambda} : lambda |- 4}. Path products form a basis of Lambda_4 (rank 5 = p(4)). Coefficients are integers, often negative (K_4 = 6 X_{P_4} - 4 X_{P_31} - 3 X_{P_22} + 2 X_{P_211}).
